target_customer: National security and defense buyers (navies, coast guards) plus operators protecting oil rigs, shipping terminals and harbors
problem: Crewed naval patrol vessels cost tens of millions of dollars, so critical maritime assets are hard to defend at scale.
business_model: Hardware sales of autonomous surface vessels plus command and control software and mission payload modules

founders.name: Ivan Avanesov
founders.background_notes: YC page: about 8 years in marine robotics research.

founders.name: Marcell Veszpremi
founders.background_notes: YC page: humanoid robot Artemis at UCLA RoMeLa, embedded and battery software at Verkada.

competitors.name: Saronic
competitors.funding_then: 55M USD Series A (2023-10) and 175M USD Series B (2024-07)

competitors.name: Saildrone
competitors.what: Uncrewed surface vehicles, mainly for research and ocean data

technical_complexity.rationale: Autonomous navigation, sensor fusion, comms denied operation and a 50 knot hull with mass manufacturing needs, for a tiny team in 2025.

defensibility.rationale: Defense contracts and Navy test relationships are slow to win and sticky, but well funded rivals were chasing the same buyer.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Bloomberg in April 2025 described Anduril, Saronic and Saildrone moving into captainless ships. No acquisition of Splash found.

market_need_then: Navies were seeking low cost uncrewed vessels, and defense tech funding for maritime autonomy grew in 2024 and 2025, with Replicator style programs. The company later demonstrated resupply of USS Essex at RIMPAC 2026 (reported July 2026).

branding.domain_note: Uses splash9.com; company appears as Splash Inc. and Splash Industries and the product is called splash9.

identity.voice_and_tone: Bold, confident defense marketing (Tomorrow's maritime assets are unmanned) with some site typos.

branding.brand_signature: Typhoon USV, the 11 foot drone boat
branding.community_and_virality: Coverage in Naval News, Axios, Marine Insight, DroneXL and others around RIMPAC 2026 and the Airstrike Pack launch (2026-08).

brand_strength.rationale: Product naming (Typhoon, Tempest) and a vivid RIMPAC demo drew national defense press, but the company name is generic and inconsistent across sources.

outcome_analysis: Splash joined YC in Winter 2025 as a two founder maritime autonomy startup and by July 2026 had a fielded Typhoon USV that completed a reported first autonomous resupply of a US warship at RIMPAC. It then added an Airstrike Pack payload (2026-08) and is preparing the larger Tempest. Funding is not verified in primary sources, so capital strength relative to well funded rivals is unknown.
notes: Aggregators (Standout, Startup Seeker) list 500K USD total from YC; unverified so no round recorded. The YC page news lists a headline Ubiquity Backs Splash dated 2026-07-21 with no amount; a follow-up search found no article, so it is not recorded as a round. Specs differ between sources (range 350 vs 800, location Los Angeles, El Segundo, Inglewood). Competitor funding comes from 2023 and 2024 sources predating the batch; Blue Water Autonomy 14M seed (2025-04) was just after the batch and is omitted.
